eyebrow: Microsoft Fabric & Real-Time Analytics · Chapter Three
subtitle: Lesson 66 · Production Data Engineering

code:
Code rollback:  revert the commit, redeploy the previous
                version through CI/CD -- simple, usually fast
Data rollback:  undo the effect of bad data already written,
                already displayed, already alerted on -- much harder
caption: Reverting the code stops the bleeding forward, not what already happened.

eyebrow: Side effects a rollback can't undo
code:
Already happened, un-undoable:
- An Activator alert that already notified a real person
- A dashboard tile a dispatcher already acted on
- A report that already used the bad numbers
caption: This is exactly why mitigation matters as its own step (Lesson 57).

items.label: Rollback
items.sub: Fast when the previous version was genuinely fine

items.label: Forward fix
items.sub: Faster when the bug is small, well-understood, or the old version had its own issues

subtitle: Preventing the next incident from being a mystery.
